newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy Ross to visit Mideast before Albright.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy Ross to visit Mideast before Albright.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Friday any visit by Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to the Middle East would only take place after an upcoming trip to the region by special envoy Dennis Ross.
U.S. officials had said on Thursday that Albright was seriously considering a visit soon, as a result of Wednesday's bloody bombing incident in Jerusalem.
But Clinton told reporters at the White House that Ross would first make his trip, which had been due to start this week but was postponed to allow Israel a period of mourning.
"When the period of mourning is over I will send Dennis Ross to the Middle East to meet with the leaders there with our latest ideas," Clinton said in answer to a question.
"It was appropriate to delay that in view of the terrible loss of life and the bombing. Then we will see where we are," he added.

"I have said all along I will send the Secretary of State to the Middle East at the appropriate time. But I want Mr Ross to go there to do the work I am sending him there to do, to get the reaction of the leaders and then we will make a decision (on a trip by Albright)," he said.
Ross had been due to leave Washington on Wednesday for meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

The trip was postponed after a double suicide bombing in a central Jerusalem market that killed the two bombers and 13 other people, interrupting tentative moves to restore stalled peace talks. The bombers have not been identified but Israeli authorities assume Islamic militants were responsible.

State Department spokesman James Foley said the Israeli mourning period was believed to last seven days and began Thursday. Asked if that meant Ross would travel at the end of next week, Foley said: "I would say that's in the ballpark."
"The Secretary will likely travel some time after that. I can't say when precisely that would be because that will depend in part on the results of Dennis's mission," Foley told reporters.

Until this week, U.S. officials had said Albright had no plans to travel to the Middle East until a regional economic summit in November in Doha, Qatar, and that even that trip was not due to include a stop in Israel or neighbouring countries.

Albright has, however, rejected criticism that she has not visited the Middle East at all since taking office in January, saying she has met regional leaders in Washington and been in frequent telephone contact with them.
